kitDescription: Yuni is a Fire rocket-launcher Defender whose Burst II has a 20-second cooldown. Whenever the team enters Full Burst, she grants all allies (including herself) a 10-second Charge Speed buff, shortening charge-weapon wind-ups. Every full-charge shot she fires — which for a launcher is every pull — hands the whole team three riders: a small DEF buff for 10 seconds, a 10-second lifesteal window that converts a fraction of each ally's attack damage into healing, and a flat +1 round of magazine capacity for 5 seconds. Her burst is a single instant area hit for 348.73% of her final ATK that also immobilizes struck enemies for 5 seconds, a crowd-control effect with no damage consequence at scope lock.

skill1.explanation: Right trigger (fullBurstEnter fires on ANY team FB, lands exactly on fullBurstStart frames — burstCast mis-keying pinned RED by frame-set discrimination), right target (all allies incl. self), right duration (600f, no durationShots), right stat kind (timing channel: S1-removal moves team totals while the charge-bucket atkPct set is byte-identical). The blind attackSpeedPct divergence is a RECON_ERROR-class artifact the blind author flagged itself.

skill2.kitLine: Restores 2.77% of attack damage as HP over 10 sec
skill2.driverSaid: heal ticks:10 intervalSec:1 per full-charge pull; no HP pool in v1 — only the recovery channel is modeled; 10s window kit-literal, intra-window tick cadence an engine-native approximation (helm H8 precedent), ⚑2 with recipe
skill2.blindSaid: S6: IDENTICAL ticks:10/intervalSec:1 encoding, ⚑-flagged ('recovery-event COUNT is an authoring choice'); S2b: dissented — recommended ONE recovery emission per charge, calling the ticks:10-on-a-1.5s-trigger shape the over-firing nearest-wrong (~400 emissions)
skill2.formulaCheck: §11: same-buff re-application REFRESHES, never co-stacks — so in game the 10s lifesteal window refreshes per charge rather than stacking ~6-7 concurrent 10-tick chains; the driver's overlapping chains likely over-emit recovery events vs the real refreshed-window cadence, but the consumer-visible outcome (crown's on-recovery buff held continuously) is qualitatively correct under both models and the HP amount itself is out of domain
skill2.explanation: The line is not dropped (the real failure mode): recovery is observable through crown's consumer in an isolation fixture (crown's own heal stripped), is attributable (zero firings with only the heal removed), and the burst-keyed counterfactual starves to zero under B2 starvation. The live disagreement is cadence: driver+S6 (same model family) converged on ticks:10 while the independent pre-op reviewer recommended 1-per-charge; both are ⚑ approximations of an unmeasured quantity, and the driver documented estimate+recipe+tier. DOCUMENTED_GAP, not a gotcha — but this is the #1 owner spot-check item.

The two S5 REDs are redacted-schema RECON_ERRORs corroborated by S6's independent convergence on maxAmmoFlat.

gotchas.summary: Lifesteal recovery cadence: heal ticks:10 on a trigger that re-fires every ~1.5s produces ~6-7 overlapping 10-tick chains per ally, likely over-emitting recovery events vs the real refreshed-single-window lifesteal; the independent pre-op reviewer (S2b) recommended one emission per full charge. Consumer-visible outcome (continuous crown buff uptime) is qualitatively right either way; the HP amount itself is out of domain.
gotchas.evidence: Kit line 'Restores 2.77% of attack damage as HP over 10 sec' + game-mechanics §11 (re-application REFRESHES, never co-stacks). Driver+S6 (same model family): ticks:10/intervalSec:1; S2b (independent spec): ticks:10 on a per-1.5s trigger 'MULTIPLIES… over-firing the consumer by an order of magnitude' and recommends 1-per-charge.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Needs measurement, not a fudge: popup-read an on-recovery consumer's (crown) proc cadence in a yuni+crown focus video — if the real lifesteal emits one recovery per refresh window rather than stacked tick chains, re-encode as a single recovery emission per full charge (S2b model) or gate the tick chain to refresh-not-stack; the driver's ⚑2 recipe already names this read.

verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHAs: every modeled line is kit-literal on trigger, target, duration, and magnitude, and both omissions (boss Immobilize, HP-pool-less lifesteal) are documented with verbatim unmodeled entries, ⚑ estimates, and recipes. Convergence is strong where it counts — the blind S6 override is structurally identical to the driver on skill2, burst, and unmodeled, and its lone divergence (attackSpeedPct vs chargeSpeedPct on skill1) is a redacted-schema guess the blind author itself flagged as possibly inert; the driver's chargeSpeedPct is the engine-native subtractive channel the SSOT describes. The 2 S5 REDs are the same redacted-schema artifact (maxAmmoPct filter vs the shipped maxAmmoFlat) and are self-refuting — under the blind author's own percent model the ammo line is inert, so its damage assertion could never pass; S6's independent arrival at maxAmmoFlat closes the question. Driver discrimination is genuine: every load-bearing assertion has a RED counterfactual (burstCast vs fullBurstEnter frame-sets, self-only scope, burst-keyed S2 starved under B2 starvation, maxAmmoPct's round(6×1.01)=6, lvl-1 172.4, FB-enter nuke taking the +50%, damageTakenPct laundering), and the two-fixture split cleanly resolves the B2-starvation tension S2b predicted. What must change for GO: nothing. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: the lifesteal tick cadence — driver and S6 are the same model family and both landed on ticks:10, while the independent pre-op reviewer argued that shape over-fires the recovery channel ~an order of magnitude; it is documented ⚑2 with a measurement recipe, but it is the one place convergence proves stability rather than correctness.
